customer.business: Wukong (a competitive work marketplace where the buyer locks a reward and an AI judge scores the entries)
customer.target: People who buy small, measurable tasks for a small organisation: copy, translation, data labeling, small coding jobs, structured research. Founders and ops leads at startups, content and marketing leads, community, event and education organisers, and web3 project ops.

segments.name: Startup or small-team founder / ops lead
Marketing or content lead at an SMB or agency
Community, event or education organiser (career centre, conference, nonprofit)
Web3 project ops or community manager

behaviours.name: Hires a freelancer they already trust
behaviours.how: Goes to a referral or a past freelancer first and rarely tries a new platform.

behaviours.name: AI first
behaviours.how: Asks ChatGPT or Claude for the draft, and pays a person only when the result is not good enough.

behaviours.name: Budget-tight, wants proof
behaviours.how: Spends small amounts and wants to see a sample or a track record before paying anything.

behaviours.name: Asks for a sample, reads reviews
behaviours.how: Checks who is behind a service, looks for reviews and a real website before trusting it.

behaviours.name: Early adopter
behaviours.how: Likes trying new tools and will run a small pilot for fun if it costs little.

behaviours.name: Avoids anything crypto
behaviours.how: Will not set up a wallet or hold stablecoins for a business purchase.

behaviours.name: Does it in-house
behaviours.how: Gives small jobs to interns, volunteers or the team instead of buying.

objections: I do not want to deal with crypto or a wallet to pay for a small task
Why not just use ChatGPT, or hire the one freelancer I already trust?
Everyone who does not win works for free, and that feels like spec work
Can an AI judge really tell good work from bad for my taste and brand?
I cannot tell who is behind this, or whether it is legitimate
The 10% fee plus the reward is more than I would spend on a small task
Writing a good rubric for each task is extra effort for me
Money locked in a smart contract from a very new, unaudited product worries me
habits: you have a backlog of small content or translation jobs nobody has time for
you check a few tools a week and ignore most cold emails
you have asked a model for a first draft of something this month
you are accountable to someone for every dollar you spend on freelancers

pitch:
Wukong, a work marketplace at wukonghq.xyz. You post a small, measurable task (copy with limits, a translation, a labeling set, a coding job with tests) and lock the reward, paid in USDC, before anyone starts.
Many people submit sealed entries. An AI judge scores every entry against a rubric published up front, and each score is public with a written reason.
Only the top entries are paid (winner takes all, or 50/30/20); the rest get a scored report. Wukong takes a 10% fee from the reward. A typical small task is a 50 USDC reward, so the all-in cost to you is about 55 USDC. If no entry clears the quality bar, you are refunded.
Organisations join by invitation, it is a new product with a small team, and it has not been independently audited. You would fund with USDC on Solana.
Try one task for free, with a small reward that the founder helps you set up.
